operations.summary: Price a link in mobile money
operations.description:
What the payer will be charged, before any prompt is raised. Safe to call on every change of country or amount: **nothing is sent to anyone's phone.**

On a link with an amount baked in, send neither `amount` nor `fiatAmount` — the invoice is authoritative and both are ignored. On an OPEN link one of them is required: `fiatAmount` is the better choice, because the payer is then prompted for exactly the figure they typed rather than one derived by converting to crypto and back.

params.description: Used only to infer the market when `currency` is absent.

params.name: fiatAmount
params.description: Open links only: what the payer pays, in the market's currency.

params.name: amount

operations.summary: Raise the payment prompt
operations.description:
Sends a mobile-money prompt to the payer's phone. Returns as soon as it is out — `status` is `processing`, never `completed`. Poll the order; the payer may take a minute or never approve.

The crypto lands at the LINK's recipient address, which is why no address is accepted here.

Two abuse brakes sit in front of this, and neither touches the merchant's account: one counts abandoned prompts per phone number, the other counts them per link across distinct numbers. A stranger abandoning prompts must never cost a merchant their own access.

operations.summary: Poll the prompt
operations.description:
Follow the payment until it settles. Scoped to the link, so one link can never read another's order.

A prompt usually resolves in under a minute but can sit unanswered until the rail times it out; poll for a few minutes and then stop rather than spinning forever. On `failed`, show `message` — it is written for the payer and will not accuse them of cancelling unless the rail actually said so.

operations.summary: Quote an offramp
operations.description:
Prices crypto → fiat and returns a deposit address.

This is step one of two. Nothing is owed until you send the crypto and submit the hash, and the quote expires — after `expiresAt` the rate is stale and submit is refused, so quote close to when you intend to send.

Send **either** `amount` (how much fiat the recipient should get) **or** `usdcAmount` (how much crypto you want to spend), never both.

Submitting the same `txHash` twice is safe: the original order is replayed with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`. Send less than the quote's `sendAmount` and it is refused with `DEPOSIT_TOO_SMALL` rather than partially paid.

operations.description:
Verifies the registration (challenge, type webauthn.create, origin / RP id allowed, ES256 P-256) and then:

- **no wallet** → passkey-native Safe → `{ walletAddress, status: "active" }`

operations.summary: Get the authenticated user's recovery methods.
operations.description:
This endpoint runs through the **verifyOtp** middleware. The request body must include ONE of:
  • `otpCode` + (`email` OR `phoneNumber`) — passwordless OTP flow (send a code first via POST /v1/one-time-codes), or
  • `externalId` + `password` — for API-key-authenticated projects where the user authenticates with a password.
Without one of these, the endpoint returns 400 with `requiresOTP: true`.

Also served at the deprecated alias `/v1/recovery/methods`.
